text: This service reads the case facts, the guarantee and scheme facts and the freshness of each data product only through the rwb-source-data contract, publishes nothing it read from a view, and keeps the FSD field names as the source field names that contract returns.
why: Arch v5 (higher in precedence than the FSD) makes the 30 views readable by rwb-source-data alone, gives the S3 row no cell to P1 and answers that everyone else asks through REST or a Temporal activity.
read: FSD S3 A1.1 and VR-S3-001-1 to VR-S3-008-1 as a statement of which facts the claim needs and how fresh they must be, not of how they are read.
applied_in: Section 2.4 constraint 1; Section 6 FR-S3-001; Section 8.2; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S3-01
confirm: Solution architect with P1, before wave 3 system test
impact: If a view stays readable by this service, the boundary test and the freshness guarantee would each need a second owner.

text: The submission of a claim is recorded on the claim as a reference, a date and the channel used, and that record moves the claim to CLAIM_SUBMITTED; where the TCG channel is not interfaced (INT-29), the guarantee officer files outside the Workbench and enters the reference.
why: INT-29 is 'not available today; entered and filed by the guarantee officer' in both the TSD and the integration sheet, while FSD A2.2 gives the feature the actor 'System'.
read: FSD A2.2 as the record of the submission and its reference, with the act of filing wherever the channel exists.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S3-004; Section 6 FR-S3-015; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S3-02
confirm: Solution architect with the integration lead, before wave 3 system test
impact: If no interface is ever added, the 100 percent inside-the-deadline measure rests on a person's entry and the breach alert is the control.

text: The claim is assembled through the rwb-agent contract as a Temporal activity on rwb-guarantee when the preparation is due, and the checklist result is used when the agent does not answer inside 60 seconds or fails the schema check, with the assembler recorded on the claim.
why: R-GUA-04 and Temporal slide 19 name an agent, the connection matrix gives S3 no P10 cell, and NFR-024 and NFR-055 require a rule fallback.
read: R-GUA-04 as the agent's job and the agent contract in DP-20 as the only confirmed way to call it.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S3-003; Section 6 FR-S3-011; Section 7 NFR-S3-004; Section 12 OQ-S3-03
confirm: Solution architect with the P10 owner, before wave 3 system test
impact: Without a confirmed call path the agent story cannot be built and the preparation stays with the checklist and the officer.

text: The workflow state is the state of record, the published claim status is derived from it at each transition and held as versioned reference data, and both are shown on the claim.
why: The five status values cannot express the seventeen states, and no source states how the two sets relate.
read: LOV-CLAIM-STATUS as the published status of a claim, not as the workflow state.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S3-001, CAP-S3-005; Section 6 FR-S3-003; Section 8.3; Section 12 OQ-S3-04
confirm: Business analyst, S3 with the P7 owner, before wave 3 system test
impact: A wrong mapping would make the case show a state the claim is not in and a report count a state twice.

text: The claim record holds the eight confirmed fields and the physical table set of the guarantee, the guarantor pursuit and the subrogation share is written with the S3 DB story; this document names those three as entity groups and asserts no field of them.
why: Arch v5 slide 18 names the three in schema rwb_guarantee, the Ownership Map and the TSD name one table, and no source field list exists for the other two.
read: Arch v5 slide 18 as the content of the schema and TSD T3.1 as the only confirmed object in it.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S3-006, CAP-S3-012; Section 8.1; Section 12 OQ-S3-05
confirm: Data architect, before the S3 DB story
impact: Without a home for the guarantor and the share, the subrogation position is a narrative and the later recovery share cannot be applied.

text: The guarantor notice is delivered from R-GUA-06 and R-GUA-28 to R-GUA-32 through the notice path in rwb-comms, with the recipient set from the parties on the case, the template from the approved set and the period timed from proof of delivery.
why: The rules that govern the notice sit in the routing logic and the TSD, while the FSD feature that owns it states none of them and rwb-comms owns the notice itself.
read: FSD A2.5 as the intent of the feature and the routing logic as its rule source.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S3-007; Section 6 FR-S3-023; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S3-06
confirm: Business analyst, S3 with the P6 owner, before wave 3 system test
impact: A notice sent to the wrong party, or timed from the posting date, is a conduct and legal exposure.

text: R-GUA-23 and R-GUA-24 stay as two rules with different from-states, and so do R-GUA-05 and R-GUA-09, and the guarantee package keeps its count of 32 rules until the authoring owner confirms the split.
why: The two pairs carry identical or near-identical text, and no source says whether each pair is one rule with two from-states or two rules.
read: The rule count of 32 as the package the design states, with the duplication as a property of the rule set rather than an error in it.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S3-006; Section 6 FR-S3-021; Section 12 OQ-S3-04
confirm: Center of excellence analyst, before the guarantee rule package is authored
impact: A package authored with 30 rules instead of 32 changes the version the decision log records.

text: The insurance claim is delivered as the Must behaviour of BR-025 and traced through REQ-S3-002 for the claim status it records on the case, and a program requirement for the collateral event is raised when the program requirement set is next versioned.
why: BR-025 is Must and names FEAT-GUA-08, while the seven program requirements of section 5.10 name no insurance claim.
read: The program requirement set as incomplete for this feature, not as a statement that the feature is out of scope.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S3-010; Section 6 FR-S3-029; Section 11.2; Section 12 OQ-S3-07
confirm: Product Owner, before wave 3 release
impact: An insurance claim that is built without a program requirement is a scope the Product Owner has not accepted in the requirement set.

text: A release of a guarantor or of a TCG guarantee runs through the approval path in rwb-decision with the level read from the delegation table at run time, and the levels quoted in the design are not restated as values in this document.
why: Temporal slide 19 gives the release an approval authority while no requirement covers it, and DL18 and BRD Q-001 leave the limits undecided.
read: Temporal slide 19 as a statement that a release is approved, not as a statement of the policy values.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S3-012; Section 6 FR-S3-028; Section 12 OQ-S3-08
confirm: Risk with the product heads, before wave 3 release
impact: A release without a level is a debt written off by a person; a level hard-coded is a policy change that needs a release.

text: The claim deadline, the preparation window and the warning window are read as versioned reference data per scheme at run time, and no value is stated in this document.
why: BRD Q-013 asks for the deadline and the quota per scheme, ASM-020 records them as reference data with Low confidence, and no source holds a scheme value.
read: claim_deadline as a field this service holds, filled from the scheme reference data, not as a constant.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S3-002; Section 6 FR-S3-008, FR-S3-013; Section 7 NFR-S3-001; Section 12 OQ-S3-09
confirm: Guarantee officer, before wave 3 system test
impact: Without the deadline the timer cannot be tested and the product's single measure cannot be met.

text: The claim is read through the published read operation once the contract carries it, and the path is the gateway's path over this service's base; no read path is invented here.
why: Arch v5 gives the service a GET, the API specification and the TSD give POST and PATCH only, and SCR-17 needs a read.
read: Arch v5 slide 18 as the operation set that the contract must have and the API specification as the set it has today.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S3-001, CAP-S3-004; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S3-10
confirm: Solution architect, before the S3 contract story closes
impact: A screen built against an unpublished read is a screen that breaks when the contract lands.

text: GuaranteeClaimFiled is published at submission and GuaranteeClaimSettled at payment or release, keyed by case, carrying identifiers and facts and no personal data, and both rows are added to the event catalogue and the Ownership Map when their numbers are allocated.
why: Arch v5 gives the topic and the two names, TSD T5.3 says none, and the catalogue numbers neither.
read: Arch v5 slide 43 as the producer and consumer statement, and the event design as the payload rule that no personal data travels.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S3-001, CAP-S3-009; Section 6 FR-S3-031; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S3-11
confirm: Solution architect, before wave 3 system test
impact: Without the events the case moves on a poll and rwb-reporting counts claims from a table it does not own.

text: The claim is classified [SENSITIVE_FINANCIAL] and the guarantor party fields [PII], the periods are held as reference data by record class, and no period is stated in this document.
why: The claim holds amounts and a party, and NFR-028, NFR-031, NFR-047 and BRD Q-012 leave the periods and the masking rules open under DL26.
read: The classification scheme as applied per record, with the period and the masking row to follow.
applied_in: Section 8.1; Section 8.3; Section 12 OQ-S3-12
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer, before wave 3 release
impact: A claim kept past its period, or a guarantor name shown without a masking row, is a PDPA finding.

text: SCR-17 is served as a gateway-bff composite route over this service's contract and the case contract, and its owner and route are recorded in the edge catalogue.
why: The FSD names the screen and no source names its service, and DP-19 makes a screen a composite route at the edge.
read: SCR-17 as a screen over the claim read and the case, with the composition at the edge rather than in this service.
applied_in: Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S3-13
confirm: Solution architect, before wave 3 release
impact: A screen owned by two services without a composite route becomes two screens that disagree.

text: The four messages this service shows are taken from the shared message catalogue once its owner is named, and the Thai and English versions are approved against the versions this service shows.
why: The FSD shows MSG-P1-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003 and MSG-GEN-001 without naming an owner for their wording, and NFR-059 requires both languages.
read: The message IDs as shared wording, not as text this document may rewrite.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S3-006, FR-S3-030; Section 7 NFR-S3-025; Section 12 OQ-S3-14
confirm: Business analyst, S3, before wave 3 release
impact: Two wordings of one message in two services is the defect the shared catalogue exists to prevent.

text: The route is named 'guarantee claim' in this document and carries no number; the number is held as reference data once the route numbering is agreed.
why: R-LIT-01 starts litigation on R4 while the case journeys call R4 the guarantee claim, and the design records the conflict as open.
read: Arch v5 slide 3 and the FSD as naming the route, and the routing logic as numbering it.
applied_in: Section 5; Section 10; Section 12 OQ-S3-15
confirm: Business analyst, S3 with the P7 owner, before wave 3 system test
impact: A route number that disagrees with the decision log makes the route mix unreadable in the steering measures.

text: Each acceptance criterion of this document is written from the named rule and its message, and the FSD criterion IDs AC-S3-001-01 to AC-S3-008-01 and the exception rows are carried as its evidence.
why: Every FSD criterion is a placeholder and the exception rows are identical across the eight features.
read: The FSD criteria as identifiers with which the requirement is traced, not as testable scenarios.
applied_in: Section 11.1; Section 11.3; Section 12 (no separate question)
confirm: Business analyst, S3, before wave 3 system test
impact: A criterion that cannot be asserted is a story that cannot be closed.

text: The volume target of this service is the program case volume it inherits and the number of claims a month, of guarantors a case and of notices a demand are carried as open, with no count recomputed here.
why: NFR-001 gives the case volume and the sources give no claim or notice volume.
read: NFR-001 as the bound of the load, not as a statement of this service's own throughput.
applied_in: Section 7 NFR-S3-008; Section 12 OQ-S3-16
confirm: Business lead, before wave 3 release
impact: A load test run at the case volume either overstates or understates the claim path, and the difference is not measurable until the share is set.

text: The change history of this module is carried from FSD v3 alone; the v1 and v2 dates and change notes are recorded as an open item and are not reconstructed.
why: The FSD v3 change note says everything else is unchanged from v2 and the copies read hold no v1 or v2 text.
read: The v3 change note as the inherited history of the module, not as a full baseline record.
applied_in: Section 1.3
confirm: Business analyst, S3
impact: A reader who needs the earlier change history cannot get it from this document.

text: The Business Requirements Program v5, the Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 and the FSD S3 v3 are treated as approved baselines for this run, and this document is issued as Draft without waiting for a signature.
why: The FSD is status In review, the Program and the Epics 3 to 8 document carry no recorded approval in the copies read, and the run records a missing approval as an assumption rather than stopping.
read: Status and approval as administrative facts about the sources, not as statements about their content.
applied_in: Section 1.1 (Status); Section 13
confirm: Product Owner, before this document is approved
impact: If a source is not approved, the requirements traced to it move when it does.

text: The service wave is 3 and the wave of the business epic E4 is 3, so no wave conflict is raised for this service.
why: Arch v5 slide 41 and the Program BRD 10.2 give S3 wave 3, and the wave map gives EP04 wave 3.
read: The two wave statements as agreeing rather than as a conflict to record.
applied_in: Section 10.1; Section 10.3
confirm: Program manager, before wave 3 start
impact: If E4 moves to another wave, this service's release slice moves with it.

text: Every release date is copied unchanged from the source and marked (tentative).
why: Template and Rules v1 U7 and DL48 fix the dates as tentative, and a date is never raised as a gap.
read: The release plan as a plan of record with tentative dates, not as a commitment of a day.
applied_in: Section 10.2; Section 10.3; Section 10.4
confirm: Program manager
impact: A date treated as fixed would make every slice a commitment before its contract exists.

text: The requirement set of record for this service is BR-022 to BR-025 and REQ-S3-001 to REQ-S3-007; the CAP, FR, NFR, AC, ROL, JRN and OQ identifiers are new in this document and trace to those two sets.
why: The BRD identifiers are the business requirements and the program identifiers are the functional ones, and neither set is replaced by this document.
read: The two requirement sets as the parents of the identifiers this document generates.
applied_in: Section 1.3; Section 6; Section 11.2
confirm: Business analyst, S3
impact: A generated identifier that does not trace to one of the two sets is a requirement with no business owner.
